prompt: Split a log into its leading "#" comment header and its body using takeWhile and dropWhile, remembering that a "#" line appearing after the body starts belongs to the body.
explanation: takeWhile keeps elements only until the first one that fails the predicate and then stops, while dropWhile discards that same leading run and keeps everything after it -- together they cut an ordered stream at exactly one point. filter would be wrong here because it would also pull the later "# not a header" line into the header. substring(1).trim() removes the marker and the surrounding spaces from each header line.
hints: Both methods use the same predicate: line -> line.startsWith("#").
takeWhile stops at the first line that does NOT start with "#"; dropWhile skips exactly that same leading run.
For the header, chain a map after takeWhile that drops the leading '#' character and trims what is left, then collect.
